chunks: ʿAlī narrated from his father, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sakūnī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

A man was brought before Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام who had stepped on a man’s stomach until he defecated in his clothes. So he judged against him that his stomach be stepped on until he defecated in his clothes just as he had caused, or else he should pay one-third of the diyah.

key_terms.أَحْدَثَ: caused to relieve himself or defecate
key_terms.أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Amīr al-Muʾminīn, the title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام in this judicial report
key_terms.الدِّيَةِ: financial compensation for bodily injury or harm
key_terms.دَاسَ: stepped on or pressed down with force
key_terms.فَقَضَى: he issued a judgment or legal ruling

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone injures another person by pressing his stomach until he soils his clothes?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal judgment of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام concerning bodily harm that caused a humiliating physical injury. It establishes either retaliatory equivalence in kind or financial compensation of one-third of the diyah, reflecting principles of justice and liability in injury cases.
